library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(ggcorrplot)




data_population <- read_csv("world_population.csv")
data_CO2 <- read_csv("CO2_emission.csv")

names(data_population)
names(data_CO2)

size_population <- dim(data_population)
size_co2 <- dim(data_CO2)


# Identifying the data types

str(data_population)
str(data_CO2)


# Identifying duplicates

number_of_duplicates_population <- sum(duplicated(data_population))

number_of_duplicates_CO2 <- sum(duplicated(data_CO2))

#Identifying the Empty values

number_of_empty_population_fields <- sum(is.na(data_population))
number_of_empty_CO2_fields <- sum(is.na(data_CO2))

number_of_empty_field_CO2 <- colSums(is.na(data_CO2))

colSums(is.na(data_CO2))[colSums(is.na(data_CO2)) > 0]

head(data_population,5)
tail(data_population,10)

dim(data_population)


colMeans(is.na(data_CO2))[colSums(is.na(data_CO2)) > 0] * 100

colSums(data_CO2 == "", na.rm = TRUE)


#Replacing the Empty fields with the mean 
data_CO2$`1990`[is.na(data_CO2$`1990`)] <-
  mean(data_CO2$`1990`, na.rm = TRUE)
  
  data_CO2 <- data_CO2 %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      all_of(as.character(1990:2018)),
      ~ replace(.x, is.na(.x), mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))
    )
  )
  
  
data_CO2$`2019...35`[is.na(data_CO2$`2019...35`)] <- mean(data_CO2$`2019...35`,na.rm=TRUE)

data_CO2 <- data_CO2 %>%
  mutate(
    `2019...35` = replace(
      `2019...35`,
      is.na(`2019...35`),
      mean(`2019...35`, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  )


# using boxplot to identify outliers

boxplot(
  data_population$`World Population Percentage`,
  main = "Distribution of World Population Percentage by Country",
  xlab = "World Population Percentage (%)",
  ylab = "Percentage",
  col = "#3a86d4",
  horizontal = FALSE
)  

boxplot(
  data_population$`Density (per km²)`,
  main = "Distribution of Density (per km²)",
  xlab = "Density (per km²)",
  ylab = "Density",
  col = "#3a86d4",
  horizontal = FALSE
) 

# predicting the population of 2030 of every country

t <- 2030-2022

r <- data_population$`Growth Rate`

p <- data_population$`2022 Population`

p * exp(r * t)




data_population_2030 <- data_population %>%
  mutate(
    Population_2030 =
      `2022 Population` *
      exp(log(`Growth Rate`) * (2030 - 2022))
  )
?options
options(scipen = 999)


#Graphs

data_top_10_contries <- data_population %>% arrange(desc(`2022 Population`)) %>%slice_head(n=10)

#top 10 most populous counties and their population number during 2022. 
ggplot(data_top_10_contries, aes(x = reorder(`Country/Territory`,
                               `2022 Population`),
                   y = `2022 Population`)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 Most Populated Countries in 2022",
    x = "Country",
    y = "Population"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
  
# top 10 most populous counties and population number since 1990-2022

population_trend <- data_top_10_contries %>%
  select(
    `Country/Territory`,
    `1990 Population`,
    `2000 Population`,
    `2010 Population`,
    `2015 Population`,
    `2020 Population`,
    `2022 Population`
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -`Country/Territory`,
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "Population"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Year = as.integer(gsub(" Population", "", Year))
  )
  

ggplot(
  population_trend,
  aes(
    x = Year,
    y = Population,
    color = `Country/Territory`,
    group = `Country/Territory`
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(
    title = "Population Trends of the Top 10 Countries",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Population",
    color = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
  
#CO2 Emissions Around the World data set to extract emission of 10 most populous countries.

data_CO2 %>%
  select(`Country Name`, `Indicator Name`,
         `2019...34`, `2019...35`) %>%
  head(10)

co2_top10 <- data_CO2 %>%
  filter(
    `Country Name` %in% data_top_10_contries$`Country/Territory`
  )
  
co2_top10 <- data_CO2 %>%
  filter(
    `Indicator Name` == "CO2 emissions (metric tons per capita)",
    `Country Name` %in% data_top_10_contries$`Country/Territory`
  )
  
  co2_trend <- co2_top10 %>%
  select(
    `Country Name`,
    all_of(as.character(1990:2018)),
    `2019...35`
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -`Country Name`,
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "CO2_Emissions"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Year = as.integer(sub("\\.\\.\\..*$", "", Year))
  )
  
# graph for CO2 to TOP countries

  ggplot(
  co2_trend,
  aes(
    x = Year,
    y = CO2_Emissions,
    color = `Country Name`,
    group = `Country Name`
  )
) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "CO2 Emissions Trends of the 10 Most Populous Countries",
    subtitle = "1990–2019",
    x = "Year",
    y = "CO2 Emissions",
    color = "Country"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()


#Correlation Analysis


correlation_data <- data_population %>%
  select(
    `Area (km²)`,
    `Density (per km²)`,
    `Growth Rate`,
    `World Population Percentage`
  )
  
  correlation_matrix <- cor(
  correlation_data,
  use = "complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

round(correlation_matrix, 3)

ggcorrplot(
  correlation_matrix,
  method = "square",
  type = "lower",
  lab = TRUE,
  lab_size = 4,
  colors = c("blue", "white", "red"),
  title = "Correlation Heatmap of Population Variables",
  ggtheme = theme_minimal()
)

#Comparing CO2 Emissions in continents

population_2022 <- data_population %>%
  select(CCA3, `2022 Population`)
  
co2_2019 <- data_CO2 %>%
  select(country_code, `2019...34`) %>%
  rename(CO2_2019 = `2019...34`)
  
merged_data <- population_2022 %>%
  inner_join(
    co2_2019,
    by = c("CCA3" = "country_code")
  )

View(merged_data)

dim(merged_data)

summary(merged_data)

sum(is.na(merged_data$CO2_2019))

#removing empty fields from 


ggplot(
  merged_data,
  aes(x = `2022 Population`, y = CO2_2019)
) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Relationship Between Population and CO2 Emissions",
    x = "Population in 2022",
    y = "CO2 Emissions per Capita in 2019"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
  
# correction btn population and co2 emission

cor(
  merged_data$`2022 Population`,
  merged_data$CO2_2019,
  use = "complete.obs",
  method = "pearson"
)

model <- lm(
  CO2_2019 ~ `2022 Population`,
  data = merged_data
)

# continent 

country_continent <- data_population %>%
  select(CCA3, Continent)
  
co2_long <- data_CO2 %>%
  select(country_code, all_of(as.character(1990:2019...35))) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = country_code,
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "CO2_Per_Capita"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(Year))
  
#continent information

  co2_continents <- co2_long %>%
  inner_join(
    country_continent,
    by = c("country_code" = "CCA3")
  )
  
  continent_emissions <- co2_continents %>%
  group_by(Continent, Year) %>%
  summarise(
    Average_CO2 = mean(CO2_Per_Capita, na.rm = TRUE),
    Countries = sum(!is.na(CO2_Per_Capita)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
  
  ggplot(
  continent_2019,
  aes(
    x = reorder(Continent, Average_CO2),
    y = Average_CO2
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Average CO2 Emissions per Capita by Continent (2019)",
    x = "Continent",
    y = "Average CO2 Emissions (Metric Tons per Capita)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
